summary: Ianthe (Ancient Greek: Ἰάνθη) is one of the three thousand Oceanids, water-nymph daughters of the Titans Oceanus and Tethys. Hesiod names her in the Oceanid catalogue; the Homeric Hymn to Demeter places her among Persephone's companions at the abduction. Distinct from the Cretan girl Ianthe who marries the transformed Iphis.
etymology: Ancient Greek Ἰάνθη — "she who delights," or linked to ἴανθος / violet (purple flower).

sections.heading: Oceanid companion of Persephone
paragraphs: Hesiod's Theogony lists Ianthe among Oceanus and Tethys' daughters. Hyginus repeats her in the preface catalogue. The Homeric Hymn to Demeter names her with other deep-bosomed Oceanids gathering flowers when Hades seizes Persephone; Pausanias also knows the hymn's roll.
She is chiefly a catalogue and companion name without a separate adventure. Hesiodic scholarship notes that many Oceanids are called after a quality of their streams.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id ianthe-oceanid is the Oceanid alone (kinds oceanid). It must not be merged with Ianthe of Crete — the beloved of Iphis in Ovid's Metamorphoses — nor with modern personal names, the asteroid 98 Ianthe, or fictional namesakes.
